title: Magnetotransport Properties of Iron-Based Ladder Compounds BaFe2S3 and BaFe2Se3 under High Pressure
abstract: The magnetotransport properties of the iron-based ladder compounds BaFe2S3 and BaFe2Se3 under various pressures were investigated. BaFe2S3 had a T^2 dependence in electrical resistivity and a normal magnetoresistance near an insulator-metal transition. Therefore, it had Fermi-liquid-like properties in the normal phase. However, BaFe2Se3 had a T^3/2 dependence in electrical resistivity and a negative magnetoresistance. This suggested that BaFe2Se3 had non-Fermi-liquid properties near the insulator-metal transition. For both materials, the Hall resistivities indicated a hole-dominant magnetic field dependence. During a pressure-induced insulator-metal transition, BaFe2Se3 had a rapid decrease in electrical resistivity above 15 GPa attributed to an isomorphic structural transition previously reported in X-ray diffraction experiments. This transition had a strong impact on the electronic properties.
summary: This work investigates how magnetotransport properties change in iron-based ladder compounds ($	ext{BaFe}_2	ext{X}_3$) when subjected to high pressure. By analyzing the temperature and field dependence of resistivity, the authors distinguish between Fermi-liquid behavior (in $	ext{BaFe}_2	ext{S}_3$) and non-Fermi-liquid behavior (in $	ext{BaFe}_2	ext{Se}_3$). The findings highlight how structural transitions can dramatically alter electronic transport near superconducting phases.
main_problem: The study investigates the magnetotransport properties of iron-based ladder compounds under high pressure, particularly focusing on their behavior near insulator-metal transitions.
main_result: BaFe2S3 exhibits Fermi-liquid-like behavior ($T^2$ resistivity) with normal magnetoresistance, while BaFe2Se3 shows non-Fermi-liquid characteristics ($T^{3/2}$ resistivity) and negative magnetoresistance, suggesting different underlying electronic states.
method: The research combines electrical transport measurements (resistivity vs. T and B), magnetotransport analysis using the two-carrier model, and structural characterization via X-ray diffraction under high pressure.
model_or_system: The physical system is iron-based ladder compounds ($	ext{BaFe}_2	ext{X}_3$, where $	ext{X}=	ext{S}$ or $	ext{Se}$). These materials are studied in the context of Mott insulating states and their evolution into metallic/superconducting phases under external pressure.

important_parameters: High pressures (up to 15 GPa), low temperatures, and magnetic fields.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on fitting resistivity data to power laws ($T^2$ vs $T^{3/2}$) to distinguish between Fermi-liquid and non-Fermi-liquid regimes; the two-carrier model is used for transport analysis.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate crystal structures, temperature dependence of resistivity under pressure for $	ext{BaFe}_2	ext{S}_3$, and general trends showing how resistivity changes with pressure and magnetic field.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares the normal state transport properties of $	ext{BaFe}_2	ext{S}_3$ and $	ext{BaFe}_2	ext{Se}_3$. It analyzes temperature dependence to classify electronic behavior (FL vs NFL) and examines magnetotransport effects, linking these changes to pressure-induced structural transitions.
why_interesting: The comparison between Fermi-liquid ($T^2$) and non-Fermi-liquid ($T^{3/2}$) scaling in relation to magnetic fluctuations is a canonical problem in strongly correlated electron physics, highly relevant to understanding unconventional superconductivity mechanisms.

In the α struc- ture, the ladder is buckled layer by layer, resulting in the Pnma space group. The γ structure has the highest symme- try (Cmcm). In the δ structure, the layer direction is greatly compressed, without any symmetry breaking from the space group of Cmcm.

Each panel displays data obtained under static magnetic fields up to 9 T applied perpendicular to the layer.

FIG. 4. (color online) Pressure dependence of n and ρ0, where n and ρ0 are the exponent of T for electrical resistivity and the residual resistivity in BaFe2S3. The vertical dotted line indicates the pressure of the insulator-metal transition.
